data.function: re-rank drop: External CAN transceiver: TCAN1043ADRQ1 (C5215847)
data.ruling: The refutation stands. The re-rank dropped the part because "holding Standby from the enable node alone needs EN and nSTB driven together, which the datasheet does not describe". The datasheet does describe it. Table 7-4 of SLLSFD1F lists Standby as EN low and nSTB low, with the wake-request (WAKERQ) flag "X", so the flag does not matter. Figure 7-4 goes from Normal to Standby on "(EN = low and nSTB = low)" and back to Normal on "EN = high and nSTB = high and VIO > UVIO". With both pins on the enable node, the part is in Normal while the node is high and in Standby while it is low. tMODE2, the time to change between these modes, is 10 µs max. The drop's other statements read correctly: Normal needs EN high as well as nSTB high; EN high with nSTB low gives Go-to-sleep and then Sleep once WAKERQ is cleared; EN low with nSTB high gives Silent. The VSUP pin (4.5 to 40 V) and the SOIC-14 package are constraints, not failures. None of these holds up the drop. Scope is function: the ruling is about the requirement that the transceiver be held in standby while the enable node is low. It is not about lifecycle or sourcing. At 14:11Z JLCPCB and Digi-Key showed the part in stock and Active. Limit for the re-qualification, which the drop does not name: the Sleep Wake Error (SWE) timer moves Standby to Sleep after tINACTIVE, 3 to 5 min (4 typical). In Sleep the driver stays disabled, so the standby requirement still holds. The verifier says the next rising enable brings the part out of that Sleep; the datasheet does not support this. Note 5 of Figure 7-4, section 7.4.1.5 and Figure 7-5 cover a Sleep entered by SWE timeout. To reach Normal directly, nSTB must already be high when EN makes a low-to-high transition. Figure 7-5 also holds nSTB low for at least tMODE1 (20 µs max) after an EN edge before nSTB goes high. When EN and nSTB are tied together and rise at the same instant, neither condition is met. After a stop longer than 3 min, the port may then stay in Sleep until a bus wake-up pattern (WUP) or a local wake (LWU) arrives. Other wirings avoid this: nSTB on the enable node with EN on an RP2354B GPIO still disables the driver in every mode while the node is low, because Normal needs nSTB high. The new verifier pair has to choose and check the wiring.
data.evidence: SLLSFD1F (January 2021, revised July 2025). Table 7-4, Mode Overview: Standby with VCC and VIO above their undervoltage thresholds, VSUP > UVSUP, EN Low, nSTB Low, WAKERQ X, driver disabled, RXD low signals wake-up. Normal needs EN High and nSTB High. Silent is EN Low with nSTB High, driver disabled. Go-to-sleep and Sleep are EN High with nSTB Low and WAKERQ cleared. Figure 7-4, State Machine: Normal to Standby on "(EN = low and nSTB = low) or VIO < UVIO"; Standby to Normal on "EN = high and nSTB = high and VIO > UVIO". Note 3: the SWE timer starts on entering Standby. Note 4: after a Sleep entered from Go-to-sleep or an undervoltage event, a low-to-high nSTB edge moves the part to Normal if EN is high. Note 5: after a Sleep entered by SWE timeout, reaching Normal needs nSTB high and a low-to-high transition on EN. Figure 7-5 note 1: nSTB stays low for at least tMODE1 after the EN edge, then goes high, and the following EN edge leaves Sleep. Section 5.9: tINACTIVE 3/4/5 min (min/typ/max); tMODE1 20 µs max; tMODE2 10 µs max; tGOTOSLEEP 20 to 50 µs. Electrical characteristics: ILKG(OFF) -1 to 1 µA on nSTB (nSTB = 5.5 V, VIO = 0 V) and on EN (EN = 5.5 V, VCC = VIO = 0 V). Other figures: CANH and CANL rated -58 to 58 V; tPROP(LOOP1) 215 ns max and tPROP(LOOP2) 205 ns max (the 140 ns typical rows); VSUP 4.5 to 40 V.
